<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m^{(k+1)}=m^{(k)}-\frac{m^{(k)}-\frac{a}{z-\sigma^{2}m^{(k)}}}{1+\frac{a\sigma^{2}}{(z-\sigma^{2}m^{(k)})^{2}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m^{(k+1)}=m^{(k)}-\frac{m^{(k)}-\frac{a}{z-\sigma^{2}m^{(k)}}}{1+\frac{a\sigma^{2}}{(z-\sigma^{2}m^{(k)})^{2}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We sweep a grid of <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-values from large <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|z|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|z|</annotation></semantics></math> to small <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|z|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|z|</annotation></semantics></math>, using each solution to seed the next (<em id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">branch continuation</em>). This ensures convergence even near the spectral edges where the Cauchy transform has poles. Convergence is typically achieved in 3–5 iterations with tolerance <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-12}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-layer: the <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>-mapping.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> identical layers, the S-transform multiplicative property gives <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{J^{\top}J}(w)=S_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{J^{\top}J}(w)=S_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)^{L}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>-mapping inverts this directly: given <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{Y^{\top}Y}(z_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{Y^{\top}Y}(z_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, we solve for <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi(w):=\frac{w+1}{wS_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)}=z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi(w):=\frac{w+1}{wS_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)}=z</annotation></semantics></math> (the <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G\leftrightarrow S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">↔</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G\leftrightarrow S</annotation></semantics></math> relation), then compute <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{J^{\top}J}(w)=S_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{J^{\top}J}(w)=S_{Y^{\top}Y}(w)^{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, and finally solve <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{w+1}{wS_{J^{\top}J}(w)}=z^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{w+1}{wS_{J^{\top}J}(w)}=z^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> to obtain <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{J^{\top}J}(z^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{J^{\top}J}(z^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>. This avoids numerical S-transform inversion, which is ill-conditioned near <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Matrix Dyson solver.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For Kronecker skip connections with fixed <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> across layers, equation (<a href="#S2.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ Proposition 2.1 (Kronecker collapse). ‣ Operator-valued free probability. ‣ 2.2 Operator-valued extension: Kronecker collapse ‣ 2 Spectral Analysis ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>) is a coupled system of <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> complex equations. We vectorize <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\in M_{n}(\mathbb{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\in M_{n}(\mathbb{C})</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{C}^{n^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐦</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{C}^{n^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> and apply Newton’s method:</p>
<table id="S2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}^{(k+1)}=\mathbf{m}^{(k)}-J_{F}(\mathbf{m}^{(k)})^{-1}F(\mathbf{m}^{(k)})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐦</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}^{(k+1)}=\mathbf{m}^{(k)}-J_{F}(\mathbf{m}^{(k)})^{-1}F(\mathbf{m}^{(k)}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(\mathbf{m})=\mathbf{m}-\mathrm{vec}\bigl(A_{h}(M)(zI_{n}-A_{h}(M)^{\top}A_{h}(M))^{-1}\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐦</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐦</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(\mathbf{m})=\mathbf{m}-\mathrm{vec}\bigl(A_{h}(M)(zI_{n}-A_{h}(M)^{\top}A_{h}(M))^{-1}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n^{2}\times n^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n^{2}\times n^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> Jacobian computed via automatic differentiation. The cost is <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n^{6})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n^{6})</annotation></semantics></math> per iteration due to the matrix inverse in (<a href="#S2.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ Proposition 2.1 (Kronecker collapse). ‣ Operator-valued free probability. ‣ 2.2 Operator-valued extension: Kronecker collapse ‣ 2 Spectral Analysis ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>). Branch continuation from large to small <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|z|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|z|</annotation></semantics></math> remains essential for stability.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Operator-valued multi-layer pipeline.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For heterogeneous layers (<math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{n}^{l_{1}}\neq A_{n}^{l_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>≠</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{n}^{l_{1}}\neq A_{n}^{l_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>), the twisted S-transform multiplicativity (<a href="#S2.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ Operator-valued free probability. ‣ 2.2 Operator-valued extension: Kronecker collapse ‣ 2 Spectral Analysis ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) requires iterating the composition <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S_{J^{\top}J}(B)=S_{Y^{1}{}^{\top}Y^{1}}(B^{\prime})\,S_{Y^{2}{}^{\top}Y^{2}}(B^{\prime\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>Y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msup><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>Y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>Y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>Y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{J^{\top}J}(B)=S_{Y^{1}{}^{\top}Y^{1}}(B^{\prime})\,S_{Y^{2}{}^{\top}Y^{2}}(B^{\prime\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> with conjugation updates <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}=S_{Y^{2}}(B)^{-1}BS_{Y^{2}}(B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><msup><mi>Y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><msup><mi>Y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B^{\prime}=S_{Y^{2}}(B)^{-1}BS_{Y^{2}}(B)</annotation></semantics></math>. Each conjugation requires solving the operator-valued <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G\leftrightarrow S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">↔</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G\leftrightarrow S</annotation></semantics></math> relation, itself a matrix fixed-point problem. The full pipeline has complexity <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(Ln^{10})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>10</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(Ln^{10})</annotation></semantics></math> per <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-point (nested matrix inversions). In practice, for <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\leq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\leq 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\leq 100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\leq 100</annotation></semantics></math>, this completes in <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> second per <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-point on a CPU.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18308v1/figures/sv_density_panel_ov_scalar_mc.png" id="S2.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/382;" width="476" height="382" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S2.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Scalar and OV theories vs. Monte Carlo singular value densities.<span id="S2.F1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Panels show four skip-connection types (<math id="S2.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math> streams, <math id="S2.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=25</annotation></semantics></math> per stream, <math id="S2.F1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{2}L=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{2}L=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=0.02</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.F1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> samples) at depths <math id="S2.F1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\in\{1,2,10\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\in\{1,2,10\}</annotation></semantics></math> (rows) for mixers <math id="S2.F1.m19" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A_{n}\in\{\text{Identity},\,\text{Bistochastic},\,\text{Orthogonal},\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">{</mo><mtext>Identity</mtext><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mtext>Bistochastic</mtext><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mtext>Orthogonal</mtext><mo>,</mo><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{n}\in\{\text{Identity},\,\text{Bistochastic},\,\text{Orthogonal},\}</annotation></semantics></math> (columns). The scalar Dyson prediction (dotted orange curve) matches Monte Carlo histograms at <math id="S2.F1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=1</annotation></semantics></math> for all cases. At <math id="S2.F1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\in{2,10}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>∈</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\in{2,10}</annotation></semantics></math>, bistochastic and Gaussian mixers develop mass near zero (spectral collapse), while orthogonal mixers preserve dynamical isometry. Scalar theory fails while Operator-value theory is able to fully catch the spectrum, regularization parameter <math id="S2.F1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> used to reduce numerical instabilities smooth out the distribution: it pushes it away from zero and reduces the spikes thus increases the mass allocated to the 1.0 mode. The scaling <math id="S2.F1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Lc_{2}=\text{const}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>const</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Lc_{2}=\text{const}</annotation></semantics></math> ensures weights <math id="S2.F1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{l}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{w}^{2}/L)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{l}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{w}^{2}/L)</annotation></semantics></math> maintain constant forward signal variance. This normalization is shown to be accurate as spectra have a main mode bounded away from 0 an infinity. </span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Validation.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S2.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Operator-valued multi-layer pipeline. ‣ 2.3 Numerical pipeline ‣ 2 Spectral Analysis ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> compares the theoretical predictions to Monte Carlo histograms of singular values sampled from finite networks (<math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=25</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> samples). At <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=1</annotation></semantics></math>, the scalar theory (red curves) matches Monte Carlo perfectly for all mixer types. At <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=10</annotation></semantics></math>, the scalar theory fails for bistochastic and Gaussian mixers, which develop spectral mass near zero (eigenvalue contraction), while orthogonal mixers maintain dynamical isometry. The operator-valued theory correctly predicts the sector-wise collapse for bistochastic matrices.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Spectral density extraction.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The spectral density <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is recovered from the imaginary part of the Cauchy transform via the Stieltjes inversion formula:</p>
<table id="S2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\rho(x)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^{+}}\mathrm{Im}\,G(x+i\varepsilon)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><munder><mo lspace="0.167em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>Im</mi><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(x)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0^{+}}\mathrm{Im}\,G(x+i\varepsilon).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We evaluate <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(x+i\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x+i\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> for small <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\approx 0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\approx 0.01</annotation></semantics></math> on a dense real grid <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> and extract <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\rho(x)=-\mathrm{Im}\,G(x+i\varepsilon)/\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>Im</mi><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(x)=-\mathrm{Im}\,G(x+i\varepsilon)/\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Numerical integration confirms normalization <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int\rho(x)dx=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int\rho(x)dx=1</annotation></semantics></math> to within <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Cayley Twisted Skip-Connections</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The spectral analysis of <a href="#S2" title="2 Spectral Analysis ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reveals two failure modes of doubly stochastic skip connections: eigenvalue contraction and eigenspace misalignment. Orthogonal matrices eliminate both—all eigenvalues lie on the unit circle and group closure prevents misalignment at any depth. We therefore constrain the residual mixer <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math> to the orthogonal group <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n)</annotation></semantics></math> via an iterative Cayley transform <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2020b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2020a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lezcano-Casado, 2019</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Iterative Cayley Projection</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Cayley transform maps a skew-symmetric matrix <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> to an orthogonal matrix via <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{W}/2)(\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{W}/2)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐈</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐈</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{W}/2)(\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{W}/2)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. The closed-form requires a matrix inverse that is expensive for batched, per-token computation. Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2020b)</a></cite>, we replace the inverse with a fixed-point iteration that converges to the same retraction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given an unconstrained parameter matrix <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Skew-symmetrize:</span> <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}=\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}=\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, guaranteeing <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}\in\mathfrak{so}(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔰</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔬</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}\in\mathfrak{so}(n)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initialize:</span> <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\,\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\,\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math>, with step-size <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> (default <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Iterate</span> <math id="S3.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> times:</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{Y}_{i+1}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\,\mathbf{W}\,(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y}_{i}),\qquad i=0,\ldots,s{-}1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}_{i+1}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\,\mathbf{W}\,(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y}_{i}),\qquad i=0,\ldots,s{-}1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">In practice <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=2</annotation></semantics></math> iterations suffice, achieving <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{I}\|_{\max}&lt;10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{I}\|_{\max}&lt;10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Cayley Transform Variant ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>). Each step is a single fused multiply-add (<span id="S3.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">baddbmm</span>), and all matrices are <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math>, so the overhead relative to the <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional sub-layer <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is negligible.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Layer Architecture</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A single linear projection produces three unconstrained <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> matrices per token from the flattened stream representation <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}\in\mathbb{R}^{np}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>flat</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}\in\mathbb{R}^{np}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\,\mathrm{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}),\qquad\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3n^{2}\times np}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em">∣</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>LayerNorm</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>flat</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}\mid\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\,\mathrm{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}),\qquad\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3n^{2}\times np}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Each matrix is then projected onto its respective constraint manifold:</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}=\softmax(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}/\tau,\;\dim\!=\!{-}1),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}=\softmax(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}/\tau,\;\dim\!=\!{-}2),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathrm{Cay}_{s}(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>softmax</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.0539em">dim</mo><mpadded style="width:0.608em;" width="0.608em"><mo lspace="0.0539em">=</mo></mpadded><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>softmax</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.0539em">dim</mo><mpadded style="width:0.608em;" width="0.608em"><mo lspace="0.0539em">=</mo></mpadded><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Cay</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}=\softmax(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}/\tau,\;\dim\!=\!{-}1),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}=\softmax(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}/\tau,\;\dim\!=\!{-}2),\qquad\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathrm{Cay}_{s}(\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The pre-mixer <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> is row-stochastic (aggregates streams), the post-mixer <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}</annotation></semantics></math> is column-stochastic (fans output back), and the residual mixer <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math> is orthogonal (norm-preserving skip).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The forward pass implements (<a href="#S1.E2" title="Equation 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) as:</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{x}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{x}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbf{x}}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbf{x}}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the stream-averaged input (a mean over the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> streams) and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is the sub-layer (multi-head attention or feed-forward network), evaluated <em id="S3.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">once</em> on a single <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional vector. The final combination is fused into a single <span id="S3.SS2.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">baddbmm</span> call.</p>

<span id="S3.F2.pic1.31.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.F2.pic1.31.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#1E293B;">Layer</span></span>
<span id="S3.F2.pic1.31.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.F2.pic1.31.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#1E293B;">Norm</span></span>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Hyper-Connected Transformer Encoder Block. Block 1 (Multi-Head Attention, bottom) feeds into Block 2 (Feed-Forward, top). Within each block the input forks into a twisted skip path (thick arrows, <math id="S3.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>res</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{res}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and a compute path (thin arrows) that projects <math id="S3.F2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q{\to}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q{\to}1</annotation></semantics></math> streams, applies the layer, expands <math id="S3.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\to}q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\to}q</annotation></semantics></math>, and gates via <math id="S3.F2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{out}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>out</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{out}}</annotation></semantics></math>; both paths merge at the <math id="S3.F2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> node before Layer Norm.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental Setup</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Task: ARC-AGI</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate JPmHC on the <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus</span> (ARC-AGI) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chollet, 2019</a>)</cite>, a benchmark designed to measure general fluid intelligence. Each task presents a small number of demonstration input–output grid pairs and one or more test inputs; the solver must infer the latent transformation rule and produce the exact output grid (<a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Model and Training ‣ 4 Experimental Setup ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Grids are rectangular matrices of integers <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> (visualized as colors), with dimensions up to <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30\times 30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\times 30</annotation></semantics></math>. A task is solved only when <em id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">every</em> test output is reproduced cell-for-cell, including its dimensions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">ARC-AGI is particularly suited to stress-test our spectral claims for two reasons.
First, each task has a <em id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unique</em> underlying rule, so the benchmark is resistant to memorization and demands systematic generalization—precisely the regime where gradient conditioning determines whether a model can learn compositional abstractions.
Second, the all-or-nothing exact-match criterion amplifies the practical consequence of partial spectral collapse: even a small fraction of vanishing singular values can corrupt a few output cells and turn a near-correct grid into a failure.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For all experiments, we use the full ARC-AGI-1 corpus of 1000 tasks, split evenly between training and evaluation (400 training, 400 evaluation, plus 200 for ablation and validation). This ensures that models are evaluated on held-out tasks with unseen rules, and that the results reflect true generalization rather than memorization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Model and Training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adapt the <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Tiny Recursive Model (TRM)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jolicoeur-Martineau, 2025</a>)</cite>, a 7M-parameter recursive transformer, by expanding each transformer block with <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math> parallel streams.
The attention and FFN residual sub-blocks are each wrapped by a JPmHC module (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3.2 Layer Architecture ‣ 3 Cayley Twisted Skip-Connections ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>): a read mapping <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> aggregates streams into a single sublayer input, a write mapping <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\text{post}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{post}}</annotation></semantics></math> fans the output back to all streams, and a residual mixer <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\text{res}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{res}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</annotation></semantics></math>—constrained to a chosen manifold—mixes the original streams before addition.
Hidden dim per stream is <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}512</annotation></semantics></math> (effective dim <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="nd{=}2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">nd{=}2048</annotation></semantics></math>).
Two unique weight-tied blocks are each applied 6 times (12 total recursive passes) with Adaptive Computation Time (ACT) halting, yielding 4 unique JPmHC modules reused across all 12 recursions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This architecture is a stringent test bed for mixer design: the 12-fold weight-tied recursion means the <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same</em> mixing matrix is composed with itself repeatedly, directly exposing the eigenvalue contraction and eigenspace misalignment phenomena analyzed in <a href="#S1" title="1 Introduction ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">All variants share identical training hyperparameters: AdamAtan2 optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kunstner et al., 2023</a>)</cite> with lr <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, global batch size 768, bfloat16 mixed precision, and PyTorch DDP with <span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> on 8<math id="S4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> NVIDIA B200 GPUs. Full configuration details are provided in <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Training and Architecture Details ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4">
<figure id="S4.F3.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18308v1/figures/arc_example2_input.png" id="S4.F3.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/477;" width="476" height="477" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F3.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="S4.F3.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Task 2: Input</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4">

<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Ablated Variants</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare four JPmHC mixer constraints, summarized in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.3 Ablated Variants ‣ 4 Experimental Setup ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The key design axes are the manifold constraint on the residual mixer <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the resulting computational cost per module.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S4.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">JPmHC variant configurations and per-module compute cost.</span></figcaption>

<th id="S4.T1.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Manifold</th>

<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Evaluation Metrics</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report three complementary metrics:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Exact accuracy</span>: fraction of tasks where the greedy prediction matches the ground-truth grid cell-for-cell—the strictest measure, directly sensitive to spectral health.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pass@<math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span> (<math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{1,2,5,10,100,1000\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{1,2,5,10,100,1000\}</annotation></semantics></math>): probability that at least one of <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> i.i.d. samples is correct, estimated via <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{pass@}k=\mathbb{E}\!\left[1-\binom{N-c}{k}/\binom{N}{k}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>pass</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{pass@}k=\mathbb{E}\!\left[1-\binom{N-c}{k}/\binom{N}{k}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Eval LM loss</span>: stablemax cross-entropy on output grid tokens, providing a smooth proxy for per-token prediction quality.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Results</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training is ongoing; the Cayley variant has been trained for approximately <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="418{,}854" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>418,854</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">418{,}854</annotation></semantics></math> steps while the Sinkhorn variant has completed approximately <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="348{,}854" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>348,854</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">348{,}854</annotation></semantics></math> steps. Both variants are still improving, though Sinkhorn’s rate of improvement has slowed relative to Cayley.</p>
</div>

transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 25.83)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" class="ltx_tikzmatrix_col ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r" fill="#000000" stroke-width="0.8pt" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) <figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Evaluation accuracy curves. <span id="S5.F5.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Per-token accuracy shows both variants exceeding 85%, but <span id="S5.F5.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> exact-match accuracy reveals a persistent gap: Cayley reaches 31.4% vs. Sinkhorn’s 22.2%.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Analysis</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Key Observations.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S5.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cayley leads across all metrics.</span> The Cayley variant achieves 40.5% pass@1 (best checkpoint at step 380,755) versus Sinkhorn’s 34.1% at step 297,805—a <math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.19\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.19</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.19\times</annotation></semantics></math> gap. The advantage is more pronounced in exact-match accuracy (<math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.41\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.41</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.41\times</annotation></semantics></math>: 31.4% vs. 22.2%), indicating that Cayley produces more <em id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">consistently</em> correct full-grid predictions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scaling with <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> Both variants benefit from increased sampling budget with diminishing returns. For Cayley: pass@1 <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> pass@1000 improves by <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+22.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>22.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+22.2</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points (pp). For Sinkhorn: <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+22.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>22.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+22.0</annotation></semantics></math> pp. The pass@<math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> ratio narrows from <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.19\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.19</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.19\times</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\!=\!1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\!=\!1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.12\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.12</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.12\times</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\!=\!1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\!=\!1000</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that Sinkhorn has higher prediction variance—it can solve additional tasks with many samples but less consistently.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The gap has stabilized.</span> At matched step counts (<math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}100</annotation></semantics></math>K), the Cayley variant held a <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\sim}2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}2\times</annotation></semantics></math> advantage in pass@1. As both variants have continued training (Cayley to 419K, Sinkhorn to 349K), the pass@1 ratio has stabilized around <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.19\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.19</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.19\times</annotation></semantics></math>, down from <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.34\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.34</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.34\times</annotation></semantics></math> at the previous checkpoint. The exact-accuracy ratio narrowed from <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.94\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.94</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.94\times</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.41\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.41</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.41\times</annotation></semantics></math>, suggesting Sinkhorn’s convergence has accelerated but a persistent gap remains.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">High token accuracy, divergent task accuracy.</span> Both variants exceed 85% per-token eval accuracy, yet task-level pass@1 differs by over 6 pp. This confirms that the Cayley variant’s advantage lies in producing <em id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">coherent</em> complete solutions, not merely better per-token predictions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Computational efficiency.</span> The Cayley JPmHC module requires <math id="S5.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\sim}2.25\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>2.25</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}2.25\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer FLOPs than Sinkhorn (<a href="#S5.T5" title="In 5.2 Compute-Accuracy Tradeoff ‣ 5 Results ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), achieving higher accuracy with lower per-module cost—a clear Pareto improvement.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lower evaluation loss.</span> The Cayley variant achieves an evaluation LM loss of <math id="S5.I1.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.643" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.643</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.643</annotation></semantics></math> compared to Sinkhorn’s <math id="S5.I1.i6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.819" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.819</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.819</annotation></semantics></math>—a <math id="S5.I1.i6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21\%</annotation></semantics></math> reduction. This <math id="S5.I1.i6.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.27\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.27</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.27\times</annotation></semantics></math> loss ratio tracks the pass@1 ratio, suggesting that the accuracy advantage is driven by fundamentally better language modeling on the ARC grid tokens.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Faster convergence.</span> The Cayley variant surpassed Sinkhorn’s <em id="S5.I1.i7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">current</em> exact-match accuracy (22.2%) at approximately step <math id="S5.I1.i7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}162" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>162</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}162</annotation></semantics></math>K—less than half of Sinkhorn’s total training budget of 349K steps—demonstrating substantially higher sample efficiency on the metric where the gap is most pronounced.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
