<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Derivation of Dyson Equation for mHC</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We derive the generalized Green’s function governing the singular value spectrum of random matrices of the form
<math id="A6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=A+X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=A+X</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is deterministic and <math id="A6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is an isotropic random matrix.
Using a block linearization and a resolvent expansion, we prove a matrix Dyson equation (Schwinger–Dyson / Pastur equation) for a deterministic equivalent resolvent.
Isotropy forces the self-energy to collapse to scalar multiples of the identity, reducing the spectral analysis to a small set of order parameters.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Problem Setup</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let</p>
<table id="A6.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=A+X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=A+X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is deterministic and <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is centered random. We study singular values of <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> via</p>
<table id="A6.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:=YY^{\top}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:=YY^{\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in\mathbb{C}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in\mathbb{C}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> define the Stieltjes transform</p>
<table id="A6.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}(z)=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(zI-S)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}(z)=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(zI-S)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">We will access <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> through a block linearization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Block Linearization</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Define the <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2N\times 2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2N\times 2N</annotation></semantics></math> matrix</p>
<table id="A6.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(z)=\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-Y\\
-Y^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mtd><mtd><mi>I</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(z)=\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-Y\\
-Y^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Schur complement.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,1)</annotation></semantics></math> block of <math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> equals the desired resolvent:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1})_{11}=(zI-YY^{\top})^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1})_{11}=(zI-YY^{\top})^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Hence</p>
<table id="A6.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}(z)=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}\,(\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1})_{11}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}(z)=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}\,(\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1})_{11}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Generalized Green’s Function</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a block matrix</p>
<table id="A6.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=\begin{pmatrix}M_{11}&amp;M_{12}\\
M_{21}&amp;M_{22}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{2N\times 2N}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>12</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>21</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>22</mn></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=\begin{pmatrix}M_{11}&amp;M_{12}\\
M_{21}&amp;M_{22}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{2N\times 2N},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">define the block trace</p>
<table id="A6.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{bTr}(M)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{11})&amp;\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12})\\
\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21})&amp;\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{22})\end{pmatrix}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>bTr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>12</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>22</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{bTr}(M)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{11})&amp;\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12})\\
\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21})&amp;\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{22})\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Define the generalized Green’s function</p>
<table id="A6.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}(z)=\mathrm{bTr}\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}]=\begin{pmatrix}g_{11}&amp;g_{12}\\
g_{21}&amp;g_{22}\end{pmatrix}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>bTr</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>12</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>21</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>22</mn></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}(z)=\mathrm{bTr}\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}]=\begin{pmatrix}g_{11}&amp;g_{12}\\
g_{21}&amp;g_{22}\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Then <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}(z)=g_{11}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}(z)=g_{11}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Isotropy Assumption</h3>

<div id="A6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We assume <math id="A6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is isotropic in the second-moment sense: there exists <math id="A6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="A6.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\mathbb{E}[XBX^{\top}]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(B)\,I}\qquad\text{for every deterministic }B\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow></menclose><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>for every deterministic </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\mathbb{E}[XBX^{\top}]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(B)\,I}\qquad\text{for every deterministic }B\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This holds for i.i.d. Gaussian <math id="A6.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}/N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}/N)</annotation></semantics></math> and more generally for left-right orthogonally invariant ensembles with the same covariance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.5 </span>Resolvent, Resolvent Identity, and the Dyson Equation</h3>

<div id="A6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section expands the resolvent machinery and proves the Dyson equation used later.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">F.5.1 </span>Definition of the resolvent</h4>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For any (square) matrix <math id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}</annotation></semantics></math> and any <math id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\in\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℂ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\in\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math> not in the spectrum of <math id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, the <em id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">resolvent</em> is</p>
<table id="A6.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{H}(w):=(wI_{m}-H)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{H}(w):=(wI_{m}-H)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In our setting, the primary object is the <em id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">block resolvent</em> of <math id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}(z):=\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}(z):=\mathcal{L}(z)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">When we split <math id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> into a deterministic part and a random perturbation, we also use the <em id="A6.SS5.SSS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">bare resolvent</em></p>
<table id="A6.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{0}(z):=\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{0}(z):=\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">F.5.2 </span>Splitting into deterministic and random parts</h4>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Write</p>
<table id="A6.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{L}(z)=\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-A\\
-A^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}}_{=:~\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)}-\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;X\\
X^{\top}&amp;0\end{pmatrix}}_{=:~\mathcal{X}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mtd><mtd><mi>I</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.548em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mo>−</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi>X</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mtd><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.548em">:</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(z)=\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-A\\
-A^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}}_{=:~\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)}-\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;X\\
X^{\top}&amp;0\end{pmatrix}}_{=:~\mathcal{X}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Thus <math id="A6.SS5.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">F.5.3 </span>Resolvent identity (exact)</h4>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following is a standard identity.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lemma (resolvent identity).</h5>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible and <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> is arbitrary such that <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B-C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B-C</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible, then</p>
<table id="A6.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B-C)^{-1}=B^{-1}+B^{-1}C(B-C)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B-C)^{-1}=B^{-1}+B^{-1}C(B-C)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proof.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multiply the right-hand side by <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B-C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B-C)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl(B^{-1}+B^{-1}C(B-C)^{-1}\bigr)(B-C)=I+B^{-1}C-B^{-1}C=I." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl(B^{-1}+B^{-1}C(B-C)^{-1}\bigr)(B-C)=I+B^{-1}C-B^{-1}C=I.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Hence it equals <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B-C)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B-C)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.  <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Apply this with <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=\mathcal{L}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=\mathcal{L}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A6.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Taking expectation (and using that <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is deterministic),</p>
<table id="A6.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]=\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]=\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Equation (<a href="#A6.E20" title="Equation 20 ‣ Proof. ‣ F.5.3 Resolvent identity (exact) ‣ F.5 Resolvent, Resolvent Identity, and the Dyson Equation ‣ Appendix F Derivation of Dyson Equation for mHC ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>) is exact but not closed because <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]</annotation></semantics></math> depends on correlations between <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS5.SSS3.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">F.5.4 </span>Dyson equation via a self-energy (Gaussian / Wick closure)</h4>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To close (<a href="#A6.E20" title="Equation 20 ‣ Proof. ‣ F.5.3 Resolvent identity (exact) ‣ F.5 Resolvent, Resolvent Identity, and the Dyson Equation ‣ Appendix F Derivation of Dyson Equation for mHC ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>), one introduces the <em id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">self-energy</em> operator <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma[\cdot]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma[\cdot]</annotation></semantics></math>.
For Gaussian (or Wick-type) ensembles, the closure is governed by second moments.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We state a standard large-<math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> closure (often proved with Gaussian integration by parts / Stein’s lemma,
or with cumulant expansions and planar diagrammatics). We use it here as the key computational step.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Assumption (Gaussian/Wick closure).</h5>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Assume <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> has entries with variance <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}/N</annotation></semantics></math> and satisfies Wick’s rule (e.g. i.i.d. Gaussian). Then for resolvents <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the leading-order contribution to <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as</p>
<table id="A6.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]=\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\;+\;o_{N}(1)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{X}\mathcal{R}]=\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\;+\;o_{N}(1),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">in an entrywise or normalized-trace sense (depending on the regularity assumptions).</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under this closure, (<a href="#A6.E20" title="Equation 20 ‣ Proof. ‣ F.5.3 Resolvent identity (exact) ‣ F.5 Resolvent, Resolvent Identity, and the Dyson Equation ‣ Appendix F Derivation of Dyson Equation for mHC ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>) becomes</p>
<table id="A6.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\,\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx\mathcal{R}_{0}+\mathcal{R}_{0}\,\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Rearranging,</p>
<table id="A6.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl(\mathcal{R}_{0}^{-1}-\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\bigr)\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx I," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl(\mathcal{R}_{0}^{-1}-\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\bigr)\,\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx I,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">hence</p>
<table id="A6.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx\bigl(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\bigr)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]\approx\bigl(\mathcal{L}_{0}-\Sigma[\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}]]\bigr)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This motivates defining a deterministic equivalent <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> as the solution to the <em id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">matrix Dyson equation</em>:</p>
<table id="A6.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\mathcal{M}(z)=\bigl(\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)-\Sigma[\mathcal{M}(z)]\bigr)^{-1}.}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\mathcal{M}(z)=\bigl(\mathcal{L}_{0}(z)-\Sigma[\mathcal{M}(z)]\bigr)^{-1}.}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">In many models (including i.i.d. Gaussian), one can show <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}(z)]-\mathcal{M}(z)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}(z)]-\mathcal{M}(z)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> in normalized trace, uniformly for <math id="A6.SS5.SSS4.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Im}(z)\geq\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Im</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Im}(z)\geq\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">F.5.5 </span>Computing the self-energy under isotropy</h4>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let</p>
<table id="A6.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=\begin{pmatrix}M_{11}&amp;M_{12}\\
M_{21}&amp;M_{22}\end{pmatrix}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>12</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>21</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>22</mn></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=\begin{pmatrix}M_{11}&amp;M_{12}\\
M_{21}&amp;M_{22}\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> is off-diagonal, <math id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma[\mathcal{M}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma[\mathcal{M}]</annotation></semantics></math> is also off-diagonal at leading order. Under isotropy,
the contraction identities imply:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[XM_{21}X^{\top}]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21})\,I,\qquad\mathbb{E}[X^{\top}M_{12}X]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12})\,I." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>12</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>12</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[XM_{21}X^{\top}]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21})\,I,\qquad\mathbb{E}[X^{\top}M_{12}X]=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12})\,I.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">This yields the self-energy map</p>
<table id="A6.Ex23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\Sigma[\mathcal{M}]=\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;\sigma^{2}m_{12}\,I\\
\sigma^{2}m_{21}\,I&amp;0\end{pmatrix},\qquad m_{12}:=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12}),\quad m_{21}:=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21}).}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>12</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>m</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>12</mn></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mi>Tr</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>12</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>m</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>21</mn></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mi>Tr</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>21</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\Sigma[\mathcal{M}]=\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;\sigma^{2}m_{12}\,I\\
\sigma^{2}m_{21}\,I&amp;0\end{pmatrix},\qquad m_{12}:=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{12}),\quad m_{21}:=\frac{1}{N}\mathrm{Tr}(M_{21}).}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Therefore, even for general deterministic <math id="A6.SS5.SSS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, isotropy collapses the random correction to scalar multiples of the identity, reducing the random-matrix effect to two scalar order parameters.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.6 </span>Closed Dyson Equation and Order Parameters</h3>

<div id="A6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Combining (<a href="#A6.E21" title="Equation 21 ‣ Assumption (Gaussian/Wick closure). ‣ F.5.4 Dyson equation via a self-energy (Gaussian / Wick closure) ‣ F.5 Resolvent, Resolvent Identity, and the Dyson Equation ‣ Appendix F Derivation of Dyson Equation for mHC ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>) with the isotropic self-energy gives</p>
<table id="A6.Ex24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-A\\
-A^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;\sigma^{2}m_{12}I\\
\sigma^{2}m_{21}I&amp;0\end{pmatrix}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mtd><mtd><mi>I</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>12</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}zI&amp;-A\\
-A^{\top}&amp;I\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}0&amp;\sigma^{2}m_{12}I\\
\sigma^{2}m_{21}I&amp;0\end{pmatrix},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">i.e.</p>
<table id="A6.Ex25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

-(A^{\top}+\sigma^{2}m_{21}I)&amp;I\end{pmatrix}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A6.SS6.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The order parameters satisfy the self-consistency equations</p>
<table id="A6.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="A6.SS6.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Finally,</p>
<table id="A6.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<section id="A6.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.7 </span>Special Case: Scalar Skip Connection</h3>

<div id="A6.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=aI" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=aI</annotation></semantics></math>, then the Dyson equation collapses from <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2N\times 2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2N\times 2N</annotation></semantics></math> to a <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 2</annotation></semantics></math> system because all blocks commute and <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> are scalar multiples of <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.8 </span>Conceptual Takeaway</h3>

<div id="A6.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The key mechanism is:</p>
<ol id="A6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">linearize <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="YY^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">YY^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> into a <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2N\times 2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2N\times 2N</annotation></semantics></math> operator,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">write the exact resolvent identity,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">close it via Wick contractions into a Dyson equation,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">use isotropy to reduce the self-energy to scalars <math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times I</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="A6.SS8.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This identifies the minimal set of order parameters controlling the singular spectrum of <math id="A6.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=A+X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=A+X</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">AdamAtan2 Optimizer.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AdamAtan2 replaces the standard Adam update <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}/(\sqrt{v_{t}}+\epsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}/(\sqrt{v_{t}}+\epsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{atan2}(m_{t},\sqrt{v_{t}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>atan2</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{atan2}(m_{t},\sqrt{v_{t}})</annotation></semantics></math>, providing more stable gradient scaling and eliminating sensitivity to the <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> hyperparameter. For the Grassmann variant, we additionally employ a <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GrassmannianOptimizer</span> wrapper that applies Riemannian gradient steps to the subspace basis parameters <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{U}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐔</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{U}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DeepSpeed compatibility.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although our framework supports DeepSpeed ZeRO-2/ZeRO-3, profiling showed that for 7M parameters, vanilla DDP with <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> is faster due to lower communication overhead. All JPmHC variants are validated compatible with both backends.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.3 </span>Permutation Basis Construction</h3>

<div id="A7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the Perm Mix variant with <math id="A7.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math> streams and <math id="A7.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=6</annotation></semantics></math> permutations, the default permutation basis is:</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Identity</span> <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1,2,3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1,2,3)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adjacent transpositions</span>: <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,0,2,3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,0,2,3)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1,3,2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1,3,2)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cyclic shifts</span>: <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,2,3,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,2,3,0)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(3,0,1,2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3,0,1,2)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Random fill</span> (seed 42): remaining permutations sampled to reach <math id="A7.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=6</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This basis includes generators of <math id="A7.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{4}</annotation></semantics></math> (adjacent transpositions generate the full symmetric group) while adding cyclic structure for efficient mixing.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Sinkhorn Variant with Implicit Differentiation</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Sinkhorn variant projects the residual mixing matrix <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math> onto the Birkhoff polytope <math id="A8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> of doubly-stochastic matrices. Our key contribution is a custom backward pass that eliminates the autograd graph explosion of the standard Sinkhorn-Knopp implementation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Problem: Autograd Graph Explosion</h3>

<div id="A8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The standard implementation records all <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> Sinkhorn iterations in the PyTorch autograd graph. Each iteration involves two log-sum-exp operations, each of which PyTorch decomposes into multiple elementary ops (exp, sum, log, subtract). For <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=20</annotation></semantics></math> iterations on <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n=4\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n=4\times 4</annotation></semantics></math> matrices, this creates approximately <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> backward nodes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These nodes produce only <em id="A8.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">microsecond-scale</em> GPU kernels—far too small to overlap with DDP AllReduce communication. Our profiling on NVIDIA B200 GPUs revealed that 55% of the total backward pass time was spent on DDP synchronization stalls, waiting for AllReduce operations to complete because no substantial compute was available to overlap with them.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Solution: Custom Autograd Function with Implicit Differentiation</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement a custom <span id="A8.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.autograd.Function</span> that decouples the forward and backward passes:</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Forward Pass.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Sinkhorn iterations run under <span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.no_grad()</span>, so no autograd graph is recorded. Only the final doubly-stochastic matrix <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math> is saved for the backward pass:</p>
</div>
