<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Backward Pass.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Gradients are computed via implicit differentiation of the fixed-point conditions, following the framework of Eisenberger et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Eisenberger et al. [2022b]</a></cite>. At the doubly-stochastic fixed point, the constraints are:</p>
<table id="A8.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbf{P}^{\top}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐏𝟏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐏</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbf{P}^{\top}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition H.1</span></span><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Implicit Sinkhorn Gradient <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Eisenberger et al. [2022b]</a></cite>)<span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}=\Pi_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbf{X})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐏</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}=\Pi_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbf{X})</annotation></semantics></math> be the Sinkhorn projection of <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐗</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}</annotation></semantics></math> onto the Birkhoff polytope. Given the upstream gradient <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{P}}\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐏</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{P}}\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, the gradient with respect to the input is:</span></p>
<table id="A8.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>Gauss-Seidel Solver for the Coupled System</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The coupled system (<a href="#A8.E24" title="Equation 24 ‣ Proposition H.1 (Implicit Sinkhorn Gradient [ ] ). ‣ Backward Pass. ‣ H.2 Solution: Custom Autograd Function with Implicit Differentiation ‣ Appendix H Sinkhorn Variant with Implicit Differentiation ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>)–(<a href="#A8.E25" title="Equation 25 ‣ Proposition H.1 (Implicit Sinkhorn Gradient [ ] ). ‣ Backward Pass. ‣ H.2 Solution: Custom Autograd Function with Implicit Differentiation ‣ Appendix H Sinkhorn Variant with Implicit Differentiation ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a>) can be solved efficiently via Gauss-Seidel iteration. Starting from <math id="A8.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}^{(0)}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}^{(0)}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

            <math id="alg7.l12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{X}}\mathcal{L}\leftarrow\mathbf{H}-\mathbf{u}\odot\mathbf{P}-\mathbf{v}\odot\mathbf{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐗</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mi>𝐏</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐯</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mi>𝐏</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{X}}\mathcal{L}\leftarrow\mathbf{H}-\mathbf{u}\odot\mathbf{P}-\mathbf{v}\odot\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg7.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg7.l13.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">13:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg7.l13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg7.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{X}}\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐗</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{X}}\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.4 </span>Convergence Analysis</h3>

<div id="A8.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition H.2</span></span><span id="A8.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gauss-Seidel Convergence Rate)<span id="A8.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the coupled linear system arising from an <math id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> doubly-stochastic matrix <math id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math>, the spectral radius of the Gauss-Seidel iteration matrix is bounded by:</span></p>
<table id="A8.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\leq 1-\frac{1}{n}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\leq 1-\frac{1}{n}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">To achieve a relative residual <math id="A8.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\leq 0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\leq 0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, the required number of iterations is:</span></p>
<table id="A8.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq\left\lceil\frac{\log\epsilon}{\log\rho}\right\rceil=\left\lceil\frac{\log 0.01}{\log(1-1/n)}\right\rceil." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo>⌈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⌉</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>⌈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>⌉</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq\left\lceil\frac{\log\epsilon}{\log\rho}\right\rceil=\left\lceil\frac{\log 0.01}{\log(1-1/n)}\right\rceil.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This yields the following iteration counts for practical values of <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>

<div id="A8.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For our production configuration with <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math> streams, <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=16</annotation></semantics></math> Gauss-Seidel iterations suffice. We enforce bounds <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in[10,50]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in[10,50]</annotation></semantics></math> as a safety net.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.5 </span>Self-Stabilization Property</h3>

<div id="A8.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An important property of the implicit gradient formula (<a href="#A8.E23" title="Equation 23 ‣ Proposition H.1 (Implicit Sinkhorn Gradient [ ] ). ‣ Backward Pass. ‣ H.2 Solution: Custom Autograd Function with Implicit Differentiation ‣ Appendix H Sinkhorn Variant with Implicit Differentiation ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>) is its <span id="A8.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">self-stabilization</span>: the factor <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}\odot(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐏</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}\odot(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> ensures that entries where <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{ij}\approx 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{ij}\approx 0</annotation></semantics></math> automatically produce near-zero gradients, regardless of the accuracy of <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐯</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}</annotation></semantics></math>. This means no clamping of <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math> is needed in the backward pass, and the formula is robust to numerical precision issues in the Sinkhorn forward iterations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark H.3</span></span><span id="A8.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Empirically, we verified that clamped (<math id="A8.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{ij}\geq 10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≥</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{ij}\geq 10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math>) and unclamped versions produce identical gradients (cosine similarity difference <math id="A8.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>) across all tested gradient magnitudes.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.6 </span>Fused Projection Optimization</h3>

<div id="A8.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All three mapping projections (<math id="A8.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{pre}},\phi_{\text{post}},\phi_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{pre}},\phi_{\text{post}},\phi_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math>) are computed via a single fused linear layer:</p>
<table id="A8.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\phi_{\text{pre}}\,|\,\phi_{\text{post}}\,|\,\phi_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\cdot\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>RMSNorm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>flat</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\phi_{\text{pre}}\,|\,\phi_{\text{post}}\,|\,\phi_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\cdot\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+n+n^{2})\times nd}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+n+n^{2})\times nd}</annotation></semantics></math>. This reads the input tensor once instead of three times, reducing memory bandwidth by <math id="A8.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\sim\!3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!3\times</annotation></semantics></math> and cutting kernel launch overhead from 3 to 1.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.7 </span>Complexity Comparison</h3>

<figure id="A8.T13" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A8.T13.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 13</span>: </span><span id="A8.T13.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Backward pass complexity: standard vs. implicit Sinkhorn.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A8.T13.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A8.T13.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T13.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"></th>
<td id="A8.T13.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt">Standard Sinkhorn</td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt">Implicit Sinkhorn (Ours)</td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.5.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T13.5.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t">Autograd nodes</th>
<td id="A8.T13.5.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><math id="A8.T13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(T\cdot n^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(T\cdot n^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A8.T13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim\!128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!128</annotation></semantics></math>K)</td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><math id="A8.T13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(1)</annotation></semantics></math> (constant)</td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.5.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T13.5.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Backward kernels</th>
<td id="A8.T13.5.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.T13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim\!128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!128</annotation></semantics></math>K microsecond-scale</td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.T13.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim\!20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!20</annotation></semantics></math> millisecond-scale</td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.5.4" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A8.T13.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Poor (55% stalls)</td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Excellent</td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.5.5" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T13.5.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Memory (saved tensors)</th>
<td id="A8.T13.5.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.T13.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(T\cdot n^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(T\cdot n^{2})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.T13.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(n^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(n^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> (just <math id="A8.T13.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐏</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math>)</td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.5.6" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.T13.5.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb">Gradient accuracy</th>
<td id="A8.T13.5.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">Exact</td>
<td id="A8.T13.5.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A8.T13.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\leq 0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\leq 0.01</annotation></semantics></math> (controlled)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Cayley Transform Variant</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Cayley variant replaces the doubly-stochastic constraint (Birkhoff polytope) with the <em id="A9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">orthonormality</em> constraint (Stiefel manifold). Instead of requiring <math id="A9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we require <math id="A9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{I}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{I}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, which provides <span id="A9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">norm-preserving</span> stream mixing: <math id="A9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}\mathbf{x}\|=\|\mathbf{x}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}\mathbf{x}\|=\|\mathbf{x}\|</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.1 </span>Mathematical Formulation</h3>

<div id="A9.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Cayley transform (<a href="#A1.E18" title="Equation 18 ‣ A.5 Cayley Transform ‣ Appendix A Matrices Manifolds ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>) maps skew-symmetric matrices <math id="A9.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> to orthogonal matrices. However, the closed-form requires a matrix inverse <math id="A9.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{W}/2)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐈</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{W}/2)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is computationally expensive for batched computation and not amenable to GPU parallelism. Following Li et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. [2020b]</a></cite>, we use an iterative approximation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.2 </span>Iterative Cayley Transform</h3>

<div id="A9.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given an unconstrained matrix <math id="A9.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the projection proceeds in three steps:</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 1: Skew-Symmetrization.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Ensure the input lies in the Lie algebra of <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A9.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}=\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}=\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This guarantees <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}=-\mathbf{W}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is necessary for the Cayley transform to map to <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 2: Initialization.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since we start from the identity (<math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{I}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{I}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>), the initial estimate simplifies:</p>
<table id="A9.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\mathbf{W}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\mathbf{W},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is a step-size parameter (default <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>). This saves one matrix multiplication compared to the general case <math id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{X}+\alpha\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖𝐗</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}_{0}=\mathbf{X}+\alpha\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 3: Fixed-Point Iteration.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The iterate converges to the Cayley retraction:</p>
<table id="A9.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E32.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{Y}_{i+1}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\mathbf{W}(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y}_{i}),\quad i=0,1,\ldots,s-1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}_{i+1}=\mathbf{I}_{n}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\mathbf{W}(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y}_{i}),\quad i=0,1,\ldots,s-1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The full algorithm is:</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg8" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 8</span> </span> Iterative Cayley Transform Projection</figcaption>

<div id="alg8.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1:</span></span>
                
                
              Unconstrained matrix <math id="alg8.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{H}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</annotation></semantics></math>, step-size <math id="alg8.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, iterations <math id="alg8.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg8.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
                
                
              Approximately orthonormal matrix <math id="alg8.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="alg8.l2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}\approx\mathbf{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}\approx\mathbf{I}</annotation></semantics></math>)

</div>
<div id="alg8.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
                
                
              <math id="alg8.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}\leftarrow\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}\leftarrow\tilde{\mathbf{H}}-\tilde{\mathbf{H}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg8.l3.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg8.l3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Skew-symmetrize
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg8.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>
                
                
              <math id="alg8.l4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}\leftarrow\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐘</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}\leftarrow\mathbf{I}_{n}+\alpha\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg8.l4.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg8.l4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Initialize (saves one matmul since <math id="alg8.l4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{I}</annotation></semantics></math>)
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg8.l5" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">5:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="alg8.l5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg8.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\ldots,s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\ldots,s</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg8.l5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>

</div>
<div id="alg8.l6" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">6:</span></span>
                
                
                <math id="alg8.l6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}\leftarrow\mathbf{I}_{n}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\mathbf{W}(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐘</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}\leftarrow\mathbf{I}_{n}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\mathbf{W}(\mathbf{I}_{n}+\mathbf{Y})</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg8.l6.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg8.l6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Fixed-point step via <span id="alg8.l6.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">baddbmm</span>
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg8.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">7:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="alg8.l7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg8.l7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
</div>
<div id="alg8.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg8.l8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">8:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="alg8.l8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg8.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐘</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.3 </span>Properties of the Cayley Projection</h3>

<div id="A9.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A9.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition I.1</span></span><span id="A9.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Norm Preservation)<span id="A9.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐘</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Y}</annotation></semantics></math> produced by <a href="#alg8" title="In Step 3: Fixed-Point Iteration. ‣ I.2 Iterative Cayley Transform ‣ Appendix I Cayley Transform Variant ‣ JPmHCDynamical Isometry via Orthogonal Hyper-Connections" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, <math id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{x}\|\approx\|\mathbf{x}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐘𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{x}\|\approx\|\mathbf{x}\|</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the approximation improving with more iterations <math id="A9.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A9.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A9.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition I.2</span></span><span id="A9.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Determinant)<span id="A9.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A9.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The determinant satisfies <math id="A9.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\det(\mathbf{Y})|\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\det(\mathbf{Y})|\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math>, approaching exactness as <math id="A9.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In practice, <math id="A9.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=2</annotation></semantics></math> iterations suffice for deep learning applications <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. [2020b]</a></cite>, achieving orthonormality deviation <math id="A9.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{I}\|_{\max}&lt;10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{Y}^{\top}\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{I}\|_{\max}&lt;10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.4 </span>CUDA Graph Compatibility</h3>

<div id="A9.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A critical implementation detail is <span id="A9.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">pre-allocation of the identity matrix</span>. When using <span id="A9.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile(mode=’reduce-overhead’)</span>, PyTorch captures CUDA graphs that require static tensor shapes. Dynamic calls to <span id="A9.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.eye()</span> or <span id="A9.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.ones()</span> during forward pass break graph capture.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We solve this by registering the identity matrix as a persistent buffer during module initialization:</p>
<table id="A9.E33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext='\texttt{self.register\_buffer("\_identity", torch.eye}(n)\texttt{, persistent=False)}' display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">self.register_buffer("_identity", torch.eye</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">, persistent=False)</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{self.register\_buffer("\_identity", torch.eye}(n)\texttt{, persistent=False)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For batched operation (when the batch size <math id="A9.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\cdot L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\cdot L</annotation></semantics></math> is known), we pre-expand:</p>
<table id="A9.E34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{I}_{\text{batch}}=\mathbf{I}_{n}.\texttt{unsqueeze}(0).\texttt{expand}(B\cdot L,n,n).\texttt{contiguous}()." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mtext>batch</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">unsqueeze</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">expand</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">contiguous</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{I}_{\text{batch}}=\mathbf{I}_{n}.\texttt{unsqueeze}(0).\texttt{expand}(B\cdot L,n,n).\texttt{contiguous}().</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This ensures the same memory is reused across forward passes, enabling CUDA graph capture.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.5 </span>Layer Architecture</h3>

<div id="A9.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The full Cayley JPmHC layer computes three mapping matrices per token:</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A9.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="A9.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A9.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fused projection</span>: A single linear layer produces all three unconstrained matrices:</p>
<table id="A9.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A9.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}\,|\,\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}\,|\,\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\cdot\mathrm{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>post</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>LayerNorm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>flat</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{pre}}\,|\,\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{post}}\,|\,\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{res}}]=\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\cdot\mathrm{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{x}_{\text{flat}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A9.I1.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A9.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3n^{2}\times nd}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\text{fused}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3n^{2}\times nd}</annotation></semantics></math> and the output is split and reshaped to <math id="A9.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B\cdot L,n,n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B\cdot L,n,n)</annotation></semantics></math> for each.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A9.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A9.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Constraint projection</span>:</p>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(38)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A9.I1.i2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Note that <math id="A9.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A9.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>post</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{post}}</annotation></semantics></math> use softmax (row-stochastic and column-stochastic respectively, with temperature <math id="A9.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>) rather than sigmoid, since the Cayley variant operates on full <math id="A9.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> mixing matrices for pre/post.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A9.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A9.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Forward computation</span>:</p>
<table id="A9.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A9.E39.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}\cdot\mathbf{x}_{\text{streams}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>streams</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbf{H}_{\text{pre}}\cdot\mathbf{x}_{\text{streams}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A9.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The final combination uses <span id="A9.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.baddbmm</span> for a fused residual-plus-write operation, avoiding a separate <span id="A9.SS5.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bmm</span> followed by addition.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">

<figure id="A9.T14" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A9.T14.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 14</span>: </span><span id="A9.T14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Properties of doubly-stochastic (Sinkhorn) vs. orthonormal (Cayley) mixing.</span></figcaption>

<td id="A9.T14.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt">Doubly-Stochastic (<math id="A9.T14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>)</td>
<td id="A9.T14.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt">Orthonormal (<math id="A9.T14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n)</annotation></semantics></math>)</td></tr>

<td id="A9.T14.5.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Non-negative</td>
<td id="A9.T14.5.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Unconstrained sign</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T14.5.4" class="ltx_tr">

<tr id="A9.T14.5.6" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A9.T14.5.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Not a convex set</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T14.5.7" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A9.T14.5.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">May attenuate</td>
<td id="A9.T14.5.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Preserved</td></tr>
<tr id="A9.T14.5.8" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A9.T14.5.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb">Backward cost</th>
<td id="A9.T14.5.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A9.T14.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(T)</annotation></semantics></math> or implicit</td>
<td id="A9.T14.5.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">Standard autograd</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A9.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The norm-preserving property of orthonormal mixing is particularly beneficial for recursive models where the same layer is applied multiple times—it prevents representation collapse or explosion across recursion steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Grassmannian Variant</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Grassmannian variant provides a <span id="A10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">parameter-efficient</span> alternative to both Sinkhorn and Cayley by learning a rank-<math id="A10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> subspace projection instead of a full <math id="A10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> mixing matrix. The residual mapping is represented as:</p>
<table id="A10.E44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A10.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{U}\mathbf{U}^{\top},\quad\mathbf{U}\in\mathrm{St}(n,p),\quad\mathbf{U}^{\top}\mathbf{U}=\mathbf{I}_{p}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝐔𝐔</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐔</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>St</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐔</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐔</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{U}\mathbf{U}^{\top},\quad\mathbf{U}\in\mathrm{St}(n,p),\quad\mathbf{U}^{\top}\mathbf{U}=\mathbf{I}_{p},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A10.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\leq n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\leq n</annotation></semantics></math> (default <math id="A10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=\lfloor n/2\rfloor" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=\lfloor n/2\rfloor</annotation></semantics></math>). This projector is <span id="A10.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">idempotent</span> (<math id="A10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{2}=\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{2}=\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}</annotation></semantics></math>), <span id="A10.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">symmetric</span> (<math id="A10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>res</mtext><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}=\mathbf{H}_{\text{res}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>), and has <span id="A10.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">rank exactly <math id="A10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math></span>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.1 </span>Parameter Efficiency</h3>

<div id="A10.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The key advantage is the reduction in parameters for the residual mixing:</p>
</div>
<figure id="A10.T15" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A10.T15.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 15</span>: </span><span id="A10.T15.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Parameter count for residual mixing matrix (<math id="A10.T15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></figcaption>
<table id="A10.T15.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A10.T15.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A10.T15.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Variant</th>
<th id="A10.T15.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Parameters</th>
